title: I'm a laid off software engineer turned game dev. Looking for feedback
author: TheRisingRonin
selftext:
Used to use Claude for building systems, and now I've been doing side projects and games I've always wanted to make over the years. I've been working on a chill roguelite autobattler with 10-20 min runs. I think now, it's close to the game I set out to make and would love any and all feedback on it.

[https://therisingronin.itch.io/hexbound-company](https://therisingronin.itch.io/hexbound-company)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/TheRisingRonin please add some details about how you used AI to develop this. Saying you used AI isn't enough on its own. We're looking for the actual dev details. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process and the actual development. We're trying to keep the sub from filling up with low quality game posts. If this doesn't get updated, it may be removed.

replies.author: TheRisingRonin
replies.body: Added my dev process, is that sufficient?

comments.author: theflossboss1
comments.body:
When people label things as AI-slop it is usually due to the art direction.  I would say at this current point your game falls heavily into the category of AI slop since it looks quite generic to what any of the big LLMs pump out when you give them a single prompt on the max thinking power.

So I would say to start there and think what unified art direction you want your game to have because right now it looks both too generic and inconsistent

replies.author: TheRisingRonin
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! I'm not the most art-adept

replies.author: Fizassist1
replies.body: I actually dont mind the game graphics themselves, but the UI screams AI

comments.author: iliadz
comments.body:
Your trailer here is just way too fast for me. It jumped through three or four screen shots super fast. I don't think those screens were needed, but hard to tell, so either make the video say 5 seconds longer, or cut them out imo. 

Also, be careful taking advice from strangers, even myself. I have another business that is quite succesful, and one thing i always tell me team, I am NOT my customer. Meaning just because I like, or don't like, something doesn't mean I am the source of truth! :)

replies.author: TheRisingRonin
replies.body:
I appreciate it! Good advice.  
Whenever I worked with UI designers, they're favorite quote is:  
*"If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses"*

comments.author: DarkHorseCards
comments.body:
Agree with the other commenters, I don't understand the downvotes though, this is a sub for this type of stuff... seems fine to me.

Take a screenshot and feed them back to the ai for different ui layout ideas.  Lots of empty space and it feels like a business app with a view of a game.  Concept looks like it would be fun though!  Just try some layout/graphic revisions.

comments.author: maxneuds
comments.body:
Change the name please. Hexbound is what AI told you because you use Hextiles. I got the same name recommended once for one of my ideas.
Same with Ghostbound and Naturebound. Claude and Chatty like these names. Also anything Ember as fantasy game name with Claude.

comments.author: BIGCHUG1404
comments.body: Things like UI and font are gonna be the big ones. When you see enough ai prompt results you get a good eye for the “default” choices that AI will pick. AI also loves pointless ui messages like “Grow. Learn. Adapt.” and “Choose your path. Watch them fight.” and stuff like that. Otherwise looks cool to me!

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/95x2gkp8yt2i1.png

Your UI reminds me of a 2010 era godaddy admin page (or a JIRA board for some of the earlier bits). You're definitely an engineer. :P   
  
The color coding is strange, I am confused by what green is supposed to indicate here as it's used on several elements in different states (completed steps, click this button to buy, active commander tab vs the tan inactive tab, etc). The small font is hard to read, doesn't give "child like" - and the way some of the type is presented is very bland to me (it just looks like its floating word processing, rather than an extension of your menu design - to give an example, the WoW quest log feels like a scroll within the menu because of the background, the ornate borders and the way the type is layed out). 

The animations are a bit off. It's totally fine for them to feel a little clunky, your characters read like game pieces to me so that would be on brand. They do seem to sort of skate around however (watch the red knight around \~10 seconds), and some of the strike animations felt sorta dull, and could stand to be a little chunkier. Try freezing the animation on strike impact just for a split second, if you haven't already. 

The healthbars and stars over them are tiny. 

Looks like a decent start, good luck!

replies.author: TheRisingRonin
replies.body: Haha, I was always better at code than UI.Thank you!
